# SRK Steel

> SRK Steel supplies mild steel, stainless steel, galvanized steel and aluminium products for UAE, GCC and selected Middle East construction, roofing, cladding, fitout, MEP support and fabrication projects.

## Buyer Guides
- [GI Metal Decking Sheets: How to Choose Profile, Thickness and Span](https://srksteel.com/blogs/how-to-choose-gi-metal-decking-sheets) — Choose GI metal decking sheets from the approved floor design, not from price or profile name alone. Confirm deck profile, base-metal thickness, coating, span and support layout, concrete slab requirement, shear-stud coordination, sheet lengths and delivery sequence. For engineered floors, the structural drawing and approved load tables should control the final selection.
- [C Purlins vs Z Purlins: Which Profile Fits Your Roof or Wall System?](https://srksteel.com/blogs/c-purlins-vs-z-purlins) — C purlins are often used where a straightforward channel section and simple-span or wall-girt arrangement fits the structural design. Z purlins are commonly selected for multi-bay roof runs because their geometry can suit lapped continuity at supports. Final selection must follow the engineer's span, load, connection, bracing and cladding design.
- [Strut Channel Buying Guide for MEP, HVAC, Cable Tray and Pipe Supports](https://srksteel.com/blogs/strut-channel-buying-guide) — Choose strut channel from the support load, span, orientation, installation environment and connection system—not from channel width alone. Confirm profile size, steel thickness, slotted or plain configuration, finish, length, support spacing, brackets, channel nuts, rods and clamps. For loaded supports, use engineer-approved or manufacturer load data for the exact channel configuration.
- [Stainless Steel Coil, Sheet, Slit Coil and Wire: A Buyer Selection Guide](https://srksteel.com/blogs/stainless-steel-coil-sheet-wire-selection-guide) — Start by defining the stainless product form—coil, plain sheet, slit coil or wire—then state the exact grade or standard, thickness or wire diameter, width or sheet size, surface finish, quantity, processing, packing and certificate requirements. Grade and finish are separate decisions, and any substitution should be approved against the project's service environment and fabrication process.
- [Drywall Partition System Buying Guide: GI Studs, Tracks and Framing](https://srksteel.com/blogs/drywall-partition-system-buying-guide) — Buy drywall GI studs and tracks as part of an approved wall or ceiling assembly. Confirm profile type, section size, steel thickness, stud spacing, wall height, board layers, insulation, deflection-head detail, fire/acoustic requirement and accessories. Fire resistance and sound performance belong to the complete tested assembly, not to the metal framing alone.
- [Steel RFQ Checklist for Contractors and Procurement Teams](https://srksteel.com/blogs/steel-rfq-checklist-for-contractors) — A strong steel RFQ gives every bidder the same technical and commercial basis: product form, grade or standard, dimensions, thickness, finish or coating, quantity, drawings/BOQ revision, certificates, processing, packing, delivery location and required date. Separate mandatory requirements from acceptable alternatives and record supplier deviations before comparing price.

## RFQ Guidance
For a useful steel RFQ, provide product name, grade or material, size, thickness, length or width, finish/coating, quantity, drawing or BOQ reference, delivery city, timeline, certificate needs, packing needs and any cutting, punching or slitting requirements.
